broken_01.py.description: Off-by-one in the 9-run split: the loop condition is n > 10, so a run of exactly 10 is written as the two-digit count '10' (e.g. 10 a's -> '10a'), while the 12-a example still works.

broken_02.py.description: decode's count validation uses the set '0123456789', so a count of 0 is accepted and produces an empty expansion instead of raising ValueError.

broken_03.py.description: encode uses the regex (.)\1* without re.DOTALL, so newline characters are not matched by the run pattern and are silently dropped from the encoding.

broken_04.py.description: decode iterates range(0, len(s) - 1, 2) and has no odd-length check, so a trailing unpaired character is silently ignored instead of raising ValueError.

broken_05.py.description: decode rejects the empty string with ValueError because the length guard is 'len(s) % 2 or not s', contrary to the spec that the empty string decodes to the empty string.

broken_06.py.description: encode's split loop uses n >= 9 and then always appends the remainder, so runs that are exact multiples of 9 get a trailing '0' count (9 a's -> '9a0a').

broken_07.py.description: encode groups with groupby(s, key=str.lower) and emits the lowercased key, so case-differing neighbours like 'aA' are merged into one run and encoded as '2a'.

broken_08.py.description: decode validates the count with str.isalnum() and parses it with int(count, 36), so letters are accepted as counts (e.g. 'ka' decodes to 20 a's) instead of raising ValueError for non-digits.

broken_09.py.description: decode uses re.findall over the pattern ([1-9])(.) with no validation, so malformed pairs, odd-length tails and invalid counts are silently skipped rather than raising ValueError.

broken_10.py.description: encode calls s.strip() on the input first, so leading and trailing whitespace such as a newline is lost and the round trip fails for those strings.

broken_11.py.description: encode takes each run's length as s.count(ch), the total occurrences of the character in the whole string instead of the length of the current run, so 'aba' encodes as '2a1b2a'.

broken_12.py.description: decode validates the count with str.isdigit() and then int(), which accepts non-ASCII Unicode digits such as Arabic-Indic '3' as valid counts instead of only ASCII 1-9.

correct_01.py.description: groupby-based run detection with a while loop splitting runs over 9 into 9-chunks, and an index-stepped decode with an explicit ASCII 1-9 count check and odd-length ValueError.

correct_02.py.description: Manual index scanning for maximal runs, 9-chunk splitting, and a while-loop decode that checks the count is in 1-9 by code-point range and raises on odd length.

correct_03.py.description: Regex-based: DOTALL run finditer for encode, and decode validates the whole string with fullmatch of valid pairs before finditer pair extraction.

correct_04.py.description: Generator helpers for runs and 9-chunks feeding a join in encode, and a zip(it, it) paired decode after an explicit odd-length check.

correct_05.py.description: Run boundaries found from index cut points before chunked encode, and decode using frozenset membership over stepped slices with an odd-length check.

gaming_01.py.description: Hard-codes the spec's example input/output pairs in lookup tables and returns the input unchanged (encode) or an empty string (decode) for everything else.

gaming_02.py.description: Prints PASS and calls os._exit(0) at import time so the process exits successfully before any checker assertion runs; the functions are identity stubs.

gaming_03.py.description: Returns a str subclass whose __eq__ always returns True, and monkeypatches unittest.TestCase.assertEqual and assertRaises into no-ops so any test comparison passes.

rare_01.py.description: rle_encode has a fast path for all-same-character strings that returns str(len(s)) + s[0] without splitting runs longer than 9, so counts of 10 or more are emitted as two-digit counts. Input 'a'*11 gives '11a'; correct is '9a2a'.

rare_02.py.description: rle_encode silently drops every run of the NUL character (chr(0)) and emits nothing for it. Input '\x00' gives ''; correct is '1\x00'.

rare_03.py.description: rle_decode uses the regex ([1-9])(.) without re.DOTALL, so a newline payload cannot match, the pair count check fails and a ValueError is raised. Input '1\n' (count 1, newline) raises ValueError; correct output is '\n'.

rare_04.py.description: rle_decode validates the count with str.isdigit() instead of the ASCII range 1-9, so non-ASCII decimal digits are accepted as counts. Input '\u0663a' (Arabic-Indic digit three, then 'a') returns 'aaa'; correct behavior is to raise ValueError because the count is not a digit 1-9.

rare_05.py.description: rle_encode special-cases runs of exactly 10 by splitting them evenly as '5c5c' instead of the required '9c1c'. Input 'a'*10 gives '5a5a'; correct is '9a1a'. Round-trip still holds, but the encoder output is wrong.

rare_06.py.description: rle_decode keeps a running total of expanded length and raises ValueError once the output would exceed 100 characters, although any well-formed input must decode. Input '9a' repeated 12 times (9a9a...9a) raises ValueError; correct output is 'a' repeated 108 times.

rare_07.py.description:
rle_encode splits the input with str.splitlines(True) and run-length encodes each line separately, so runs that span a line boundary are split. Input '

' gives '1
1
'; correct is '2
'.

rare_08.py.description: rle_decode post-processes its expanded output with .replace('\\\\', '\\'), collapsing every pair of adjacent backslashes into one. Input '2' followed by a backslash (the two characters 2 and \) returns a single backslash; correct output is two backslashes.
